summary: The Petitioner, Power Exchange India Limited (PXIL), has filed the instant Petition under Regulations 54, 55 and 56 of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Power Market) Regulations, 2021 seeking approval of the Commission to grant additional time for compliance with the ownership structure of the Petitioner in order to achieve the compliances set out under Regulation 15 of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Power Market) Regulations, 2021 (‘PMR, 2021’). Order in Petition No. 413/MP/2024 & 6/RP/2025 Page **1** of **12** _“(a) Pass an Order granting time till 31.09.2026 for alignment of ownership structure of the Petitioner as per the prescribed norms under the Regulation 15 of the PMR, 2021; and_ _(b) Pass any such other order or grant reliefs, which this Hon’ble Commission may deem fit in the facts and circumstances of the present case in favour of the Petitioner.”_ Order in Petition No. 413/MP/2024 & 6/RP/2025 Page **2** of **12** Order in Petition No. 413/MP/2024 & 6/RP/2025 Page **3** of **12** had observed that Regulation 15(2) of the PMR, 2021, provided a period of one year for the existing Power Exchanges for aligning their ownership structure as per the requirement under Regulation 15(1). Thereafter, by order dated 26.4.2022 in Petition No. 285/MP/2021, the Petitioner was granted an extended time up to 31.3.2023 to align its ownership structure as per the prescribed norms. Since the Petitioner was unable to align its ownership structure even by the above-extended timeline, it approached the Commission by way of Petition No. 95/MP/2023, and vide order dated 20.11.2023, the Commission again granted an additional time up to 30.9.2024. In the said order, it was also amply clarified that in case the Petitioner fails to achieve the required shareholding patterns by the timelines stipulated therein, the Commission shall be constrained to initiate measures as may be deemed appropriate in accordance with the provisions of PMR, 2021. However, the Petitioner again approached the Commission seeking an extension for the third time, thus demonstrating a lackadaisical approach on the part of the Petitioner and/or its shareholder(s) to the compliance set out under PMR, 2021, and the extensions previously given by the Commission. However, keeping in consideration the overall facts & circumstances, the Commission deemed it appropriate to give a final extension of three months from the issuance of the ROP for compliance with the ownership structure of the Petitioner as prescribed in Regulation 15 of the PMR, 2021 with imposition of penalty of Rs.1,00,000/-, which shall be deposited by the Petitioner within two weeks. The Commission also expressly clarified that the failure to comply with the prescribed ownership structure within the above-mentioned timeline shall entail stringent actions, including but not limited to the suspension of its operations. 7. Vide Record of Proceedings for the hearing 21.1.2025, the Petitioner was directed to file a compliance affidavit indicating the status of compliance with the ownership structure 8. During the course of the hearing, the learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that vide Record of Proceedings for the hearing dated 21.1.2025, the Petitioner was granted a final extension of three months for the compliance with the ownership structure as prescribed in the Regulation 15 of the PMR, 2021 with a levy of penalty of Rs. 1 lakh to be deposited within two weeks. Pursuant to the said Record of Proceedings, the ownership structure of the Petitioner has now been revised and is duly compliant with Regulation 15 of the PMR, 2021. Learned counsel also submitted that the Petitioner is praying for the recall of the Record of Proceedings for the hearing dated 21.1.2025 and has moved a Review Petition (Diary No. 191/2025), which may also be dealt with while passing the order in this case itself. 9. We have considered the submissions of the Petitioner and perused the documents on record. Through this Petition, the Petitioner has prayed for the grant of time till 31.9.2026 for alignment of the ownership structure of the Petitioner in terms of Regulation 15 of the PMR, 2021 _._ Regulation 15 of the PMR, 2021 stipulates the ownership structure of the Power Exchanges as under: Order in Petition No. 413/MP/2024 & 6/RP/2025 Page **6** of **12** Order in Petition No. 413/MP/2024 & 6/RP/2025 Page **7** of **12** Order in Petition No. 413/MP/2024 & 6/RP/2025 Page **8** of **12** 16. The Commission notes that the Petitioner, Power Exchange India Limited (PXIL), failed to comply with the direction issued by the Commission to submit a compliance affidavit within the stipulated time. The said compliance was ultimately made on 21.3.2025 and was communicated vide the Petitioner’s letter dated 24.3.2025, and an affidavit dated 3.4.2025 was submitted in the matter, thereby indicating a substantial delay in adhering to the Commission’s referenced directives. aggrieved by a direction, decision, or order of the Commission, from which no appeal has been preferred, shall file a review petition within forty days from the date such direction, decision, or order was issued. This period can be extended or curtailed if the party is able to show sufficient reasons. 24. The Review Petitioner has not been diligent enough in filing the Review Petitions within the stipulated time. We are of the considered view that the Review Petitioner has not made out any sufficient cause for condonation of delay. Accordingly, the delay in filing the Review Petition has not been condoned. 25. Petition No. 413/MP/2024, along with the Review Petition No. 6/RP/2025, stands disposed of in terms of the above.
title: Petition under Regulations 54, 55 and 56 of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Power Market) Regulations, 2021 for seeking grant of additional time period for compliance of ownership structure of Petitioner in order to achieve the compliances set out under Regulation 15 of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Power Market) Regulations, 2021. Power Exchange India Limited
